title: Vectors | Chapter 1, Essence of linear algebra
beats: Vector is the root building block; three views: physics arrow, CS list, math abstract
Defer the abstract view; pick arrows rooted at origin as default mental image
Walk through coordinate system; coordinates as walking instructions
Vertical bracket column convention to separate vectors from points; 3D adds z
Addition tip-to-tail, justified as step after step; tied to number line 2+5
Numeric example (1,2)+(3,-1): reorder steps, componentwise addition
Scaling by 2, 1/3, -1.8 shown, then 'scalar' named, then componentwise rule
Value is translation between views; data analysts, graphics programmers, his own animations

theory: The video chooses a single concrete picture (arrow at origin) and treats numbers as a translation layer, not the subject. Definitions are justified by meaning (steps you take) before being turned into component rules.
velocity: Scene builder should default to one geometric picture with a visible numeric twin, and animate translation between them
Voice should name a term only after the demo has shown it (scalar at 7:17)
Learner model could track which 'view' (arrow, list, abstract) a learner holds
quote: The usefulness of linear algebra is the ability to translate back and forth
